diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above

issues.failure_explanation: c_Omega contains max_j ||Omega_j|| twice, so c_Omega^2 scales like ||Omega_j||^4 ≈ 16b^2. The cited union bounds give (dn-bd^2)^3 δ^{-4}(2√b+…)^4, not the first power. For fixed δ (e.g. 0.2) and large b, c_Omega^2 ≳ const·b^5 with high probability, while the stated bound is O(b^{3.5}), so the statement is false. The quoted tail bound also contains sqrt(2 log(δ/2)), which is undefined for δ<2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Raise the factor (2√b+√(2log(2(m-d)/δ))) to the fourth power and correct the Gaussian tail bound to use log(2/δ) (or log(1/δ)).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit high-probability bound on the prefactor c_Omega in Theorem thm:sb is incorrect as stated.
issues.title: Probabilistic bound on c_Omega^2 has the wrong power of the norm factor
issues.why_classification: This is a local, forced correction. The prefactor remains polynomial in n, b and 1/δ, and the structural bound and the absorbed constant in conj:sb are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notably, $\Lambda$ may consist of either a cluster of interior eigenvalues or a subset of exterior eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:boundMP bounds ||Φ(B_0)|| by the maximum of ||Φ(λ)|| over the convex hull of B_0's eigenvalues. For interior clusters, a block Λ_j of Λ_⊥ can have eigenvalues on both sides of the cluster. Its hull then contains the cluster interval, where ||Φ(λ)|| is not controlled by G_d, so the displayed bound over the set [λmin,λmax] minus the cluster interval does not follow from the lemma as stated.

failure_location.quote: Note that all eigenvalues of $B_{j}$ for $d+1\leq j\leq m$ are in $[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\setminus [\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$, \cref{lem:boundMP} yields that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate lem:boundMP with the maximum over any set containing the eigenvalues of B_0. Its proof already only evaluates φ_j at the eigenvalues.
issues.overall_effect: Inequality eq:mainsb is not justified as written for interior clusters whose Λ_⊥ block partition straddles the cluster.
issues.title: Lemma lem:boundMP applied outside its stated interval in the interior-eigenvalue case
issues.why_classification: A one-line restatement of the lemma, already supported by its proof, restores the step with no change to any conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under mild spectral gap assumptions---specifically, the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$---we provide a structural bound

issues.failure_explanation: gap>0 requires splitting the bd desired eigenvalues into d blocks of exactly b each, so that no eigenvalue value appears in two blocks. Multiplicity ≤ b does not guarantee this. Example: b=3, d=2, three distinct eigenvalues each of multiplicity 2. Every split into two blocks of size 3 separates some pair, so gap=0, and thm:sb never applies even though all multiplicities are ≤ b.

failure_location.quote: The assumption \cref{eq:aspgap} essentially requires that the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis as the existence of a partition into b-blocks with pairwise disjoint spectra; note that this is stronger than multiplicity ≤ b.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the structural bound (multiplicity ≤ b) is broader than what thm:sb covers.
issues.title: Gap assumption is not equivalent to multiplicity at most b
issues.why_classification: Only the prose description of the hypothesis changes; the theorem and its proof are untouched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $d = 1$, \cref{cor:eig} recovers the convergence result for randomized single-vector Lanczos method

issues.failure_explanation: thm:sb plus conj:chi give tan ≤ c_Omega(χ/gap)^{d-1}. The prefactor c_Omega can be absorbed into c_{b,d,n}^{d-1} only when d≥2. For d=1 the stated bound reads tan∠(range(Q),K_1)≤1. In fact tan∠ = ||Ω_⊥Ω_1^{-1}||, which is typically of order √n. The d=1 remark on cor:eig is therefore also wrong; d=1 is the large-block case, not single-vector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound as c'_{b,d,n}(c_{b,d,n}/gap)^{d-1} with an explicit prefactor, or restrict to d≥2. Rephrase the cor:eig remark to b=1.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional bound and its use in cor:eig are invalid in the d=1 case, and the claimed recovery of the single-vector result is incorrect.
issues.title: Corollary of conjecture drops the prefactor; false for d=1
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate-case fix with a local restatement; the conditional result for d≥2 is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we fix $\alpha = 1$ and vary the cluster radius as $\beta = 2^{-i}$ for $i = 1,\dotsc,12$
The results show that $\tan\angle (\range(Q),\mathcal{K}_{d}(A,\Omega))$ is independent of $\beta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The top of cluster k is (αk+β(k+1))/60 and the bottom of cluster k+1 is (α(k+1)+βk)/60. The gap is therefore (α−β)/60, not α/60. In experiment 1 (α=1, β up to 1/2) the gap is not fixed: it varies by up to a factor 2 as β changes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the gap to (α−β)/60 and interpret experiment 1 accordingly, or shift the intervals so that the gap is exactly α/60.
issues.overall_effect: The experiment-1 interpretation (β varied with the gap held fixed) is inaccurate.
issues.title: Experimental inter-cluster gap misstated
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the setup description; the empirical support is essentially preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory

issues.failure_explanation: χ_mono compares ||μI−B_i|| with ||μI−Λ_i||. Take b=2 and Λ_i=diag(1,1+ε) with μ=λ^cl_min=1. The ratio equals ||Ω_i^{-1}e_2||·||e_2^TΩ_i||, which is unbounded for ill-conditioned Ω_i, while κ(B_i)→1 as ε→0. The valid bound is χ_mono ≤ max_i ||Ω_i||·||Ω_i^{-1}||.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by max_i κ(Ω_i), which follows from μI−B_i=Ω_i^{-1}(μI−Λ_i)Ω_i and is controllable by Gaussian random matrix theory.
issues.overall_effect: The d=2 illustration states an incorrect bound for χ_mono.
issues.title: Bound of chi_mono by the condition number of B_i is false
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction preserves the qualitative point of the discussion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Future work will focus on establishing a rigorous probabilistic bound to support the conjectured results.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the paper achieves Meyer et al.'s conjecture that matvec complexity is linear in target rank for any block size. The paper only gives cor:lr conditionally on conj:chi, which is unproven. The resulting matvec count b·ℓ involves bd·log(c_{b,d,n}/gap), where c_{b,d,n} absorbs c_Omega^{1/(d-1)} and has unspecified growth in b, d and n. Linear scaling therefore holds only under further unstated assumptions on c_{b,d,n}.

failure_location.quote: As a consequence, it achieves the conjecture

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as conditional on conj:chi and on c_{b,d,n} having a suitably mild (e.g. polynomial) growth.
issues.overall_effect: Overstates the paper's contribution regarding an open complexity conjecture.
issues.title: Claim to achieve the Meyer et al. conjecture rests on unproven conjecture and unspecified constant
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws the claim of settling the conjecture; only a conditional, weaker statement survives.
